question: Languages that got tea by sea mostly say te; by land, cha. Why does seafaring Portugal say chá?
options: It borrowed Persian chay on the way
Its sailors learned it in Goa
Its traders bought tea through Macau
answer: Its traders bought tea through Macau. The real divide is not sea against land but which Chinese speech supplied the word. Dutch ships loaded at Hokkien-speaking ports, where tea is te, and spread thé and Tee across Europe. Macau speaks Cantonese, where it is cha, so Portuguese took chá.
move: When a rule has an exception, look for what really drove the rule.
trap: Reading cha as proof of a land route, and so through Persia.
source: Dahl, World Atlas of Language Structures, 2013
reference: Dahl, Tea, in Dryer & Haspelmath (eds), The World Atlas of Language Structures Online, chapter 138, Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, 2013
